newsitem.title: USA: Ohio farmers planted 33 pct of corn crop last week.
newsitem.headline: Ohio farmers planted 33 pct of corn crop last week.

text.p: Corn planting accelerated in Ohio to a near-record pace in the week ended April 27 with 39 percent of the crop planted, up from 6 percent a week earlier, the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service said.

With six days suitable for fieldwork last week, planting of soybeans and oats also proceeded rapidly, it said. Soil temperatures remain too cold for germination, however, with growing degree days averaging just half of normal in the week.
Both corn and soybeans need soil temperatures of at least 50 degrees F to enable germination.
More than two-thirds of winter wheat was rated in fair to good condition, 10 percent was rated excellent and 15 percent was rated poor or very poor, slightly better than last week.
Wheat jointed 21 pct versus 12 a week ago, 19 a year ago and 16 on a five-year average.
Corn planted 39 pct vs 6 w/a, 4 y/a, 8 avge.
Oats planted 80 pct vs 63 w/a, 41 y/a, 49 avge.
Oats emerged 38 pct vs 15 w/a, 12 y/a, 21 avge.
Topsoil moisture levels were rated 8 percent surplus
